messages:
ken: Heads-up — last 20m we've seen a spike in GPU alerts coming from the DCGM exporter across eu-west clusters. Mostly ECC_CORRECTED and some Xid entries, but they're noisy and triggering node-level criticals. Anyone else seeing it?

maria: saw the same in staging earlier. pattern: short bursts from one card on nodes-3a/3b, then fades. looks like flapping not full failure.

aj: yep. alerts are blowing up alertmanager and paging infra on-call. current rule has for: 1m and fires critical on any ECC_CORRECTED > 0. Too aggressive.

ken: Agree — we should tune before we start draining a bunch of nodes. Proposal: create a lower-severity "gpu-noise" alert for single transient ECC_CORRECTED events and only escalate to critical if the same GPU reports >3 events in a 15m window or if ECC_UNCORRECTED or XidCritical appear.

liam: I like that. Also would help to route noise to a low-urgency Slack channel (eng-infra-gpu-noise) instead of paging, so on-call can choose to act.

aj: here's a quick prometheus rule sketch — don't copy blindly but shows the idea:

```yaml
- alert: GPU_ECC_Noise
  expr: sum_over_time(dcgm_ecc_corrected_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[15m]) > 0
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: info
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU ECC corrected events (noise)"

- alert: GPU_ECC_Repeating
  expr: sum by(gpu_uuid)(increase(dcgm_ecc_corrected_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[15m])) > 3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU ECC corrected repeating (>3 in 15m)"

- alert: GPU_XID_Severe
  expr: increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total{job="dcgm-exporter", level="critical"}[10m]) > 0
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "Xid critical error on GPU"
```

maria: two operational notes: 1) use gpu_uuid label to avoid node-level dedupe destroying signal for multi-GPU nodes. 2) add recording rules to pre-aggregate by gpu_uuid so Prometheus queries are cheaper.

ken: Good call. Also add a change() or increases() check to avoid one-off spikes from running batch jobs that stress ECC. Maybe exclude the job label for known stress tests.

aj: We should also add a short suppression window in Alertmanager for repeated identical noise from the same gpu_uuid to avoid flood of notifications. Route to eng-infra-gpu-noise for severity=info, to #oncall for warning/critical.

liam: On the drain/replace side — we still want automation when Xid_Severe fires. Suggested flow: Xid_Severe -> cordon+drain with a tag 'gpu-flaky' and enqueue hardware-replacement ticket automatically after drain completes. For repeating ECC_Repeating at warning for >24h mark node for scheduled maintenance.

ken: That makes sense. Need to check capacity impact — mass drains in eu-west during peak could exhaust spare pool. Let's add a pre-check in the automation: only proceed if spare_capacity > 10% in region, else escalate to infra-runbook and reduce automation to manual.

maria: I'll open a small RFC with the prometheus rules, alertmanager routes, and the automation flow. Will include test playbook: synthetic exporter events to simulate noise vs real failure.

aj: small nit: use sum_over_time(dcgm_ecc_corrected_total[15m]) vs increase() depending on exporter counter semantics. We'll validate in staging.

sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026 — "GPU alert storm — tuning & routing". Owners: @maria, @aj.

liam: Thanks — if you want me to own automation checkpoints I can pair with @maria this afternoon. :thumbsup:

ken: Great. Maria, assign RFC to review by EOD tomorrow. Let's aim to roll rule changes in staging tonight and monitor for 24h before prod.

maria: Will do. test harness ready. I'll post updates in this thread after staging run. :rocket:
